question: In July 2023, the Commission signed a memorandum of understanding on a partnership with Tunisia that includes migration. Human Rights and media organisations have reported the repeated practice, employed by some Tunisian coastguards, of dismantling the engine of intercepted migrant boats and leaving the migrants adrift at sea. 1.

Does the Commission know whether Tunisian coastguards will be formally trained on such practices as part of the ‘Strengthening the Tunisian coast guard training pillar’ project coordinated by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development?

Does the Commission have any indication whether Tunisian coastguards have been infiltrated by criminal groups, as Libyan coastguards have been, as noted by EU Commissioner Ylva Johansson in a statement on 6 July 2023?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.4.2024) On 16 July 2023, the EU and Tunisia signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU)1 for a strategic and global partnership based on five pillars – macroeconomic stability, trade and investment, green energy transition, people-to-people contacts and migration and mobility.

The MoU complements the EU–Tunisia Association Agreement2 and Member States' bilateral initiatives, and prioritises measures against irregular migration, including antismuggling operations, border management and returns, with a view to avoiding loss of human lives and developing legal pathways for migration.

One element of EU support in the area of border management is to strengthen the training pillar of the Tunisian coast guard. As to date, the Tunisian coast guard has not had an established training academy, a specific training academy will be established through EU funding, including revision of the training curriculum and provision of capacity-building.

The Tunisian coast guard will be also trained on human rights, rule of law principles and international standards. Modules on these subjects will be included in the training curriculum to ensure its sustainability. The programme is being implemented by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development3, also supported by technical expertise from the German federal police and started in January 2023.

Currently, the training curricula and the overall structure of the academy are under discussion with the Tunisian authorities (number of years of training, type/level of studies envisaged, design of the academy’s building).
